picks.title: Suno brings its voice clone tool to iOS and Android, opens a limited version to free users
picks.excerpt: Suno's Voices feature — record or upload yourself singing, then generate new songs in your own voice — is now on iOS and Android, with a limited version opened to free users. Consented self-cloning moves from a paid desktop experiment to a default mobile capability.
picks.rationale: Consented voice cloning becomes a free, phone-native default — the most concrete change in how anyone can make vocals tomorrow.

picks.title: Can AI Unlearn Music? What Musicians Need to Know
picks.excerpt: AI companies increasingly promise they can "unlearn" a musician's work after training, but the new Machine Unlearning Research Hub argues that removing data from a trained model is largely infeasible today. Hypebot translates the research into what an artist should actually ask for when a platform offers opt-out.
picks.rationale: Turns a research finding into a negotiating checklist — what an opt-out or takedown promise can and cannot deliver.

picks.title: HeadRush rolls out Tone3000 integration and native support for NAM captures on its amp and effects modellers
picks.excerpt: HeadRush 5.1 adds native Neural Amp Modeler capture support and Tone3000 integration to its Prime modellers, letting players load "hundreds of thousands" of community-trained neural amp captures straight onto the rig. Neural tone-cloning stops being a nerd side-project and becomes a stock feature of mainstream guitar hardware.
picks.rationale: An open neural-capture format lands as a stock firmware feature on mainstream hardware — a shipping update players can install now.

picks.title: Saregama is using AI to make music videos for songs whose visuals it never owned
picks.excerpt: Saregama, India's oldest label, is generating AI music videos for catalogue songs whose original visuals it never owned, repackaging decades of audio-only recordings for Gen Z feeds. A concrete production-design use case for generative video sitting on top of a legacy music catalogue.
picks.rationale: A real production pipeline where generative video gives an audio-only catalogue new visual identity — the clearest design-side use case in the pool.

picks.title: How AI Agents Are Quietly Automating Music Companies: From A&R to Release Ops
picks.excerpt: AI agents are quietly taking over the back office of music companies — delivery QC, metadata cleanup, trend monitoring and even early A&R screening. DMN separates what is actually shipping from what is still a pitch deck, with a look at how release ops teams are restructuring around it.
picks.rationale: The only workflow-side story in the pool: which release-ops tasks agents are actually taking over, and which are still vapour.
